title: the WSG jumping rules
audit_comment: The jumping slice pins the any-character rule, the four-foot running advantage with its 20-foot straight run, the half-height high jump with the roll-to-absorb landing, the thin-barrier high jump plus Dexterity Check with the 1d3 heap damage at five feet or higher and the next-round stand-up, the per-jump die roll, Table 22 (the seven level bands with the standing broad, running broad and high jump dice), and the cumulative modifiers (moderate -1, heavy -2 and cannot high jump, severe cannot jump at all, halfling -1 broad only, gnome or dwarf -2 broad and -1 high) with the 2-foot broad and 1-foot high floors (rules/wsgjump.h, prefix wjp); census 372 -> 373.

banner.title: The WSG JUMPING, R448: the jumping prose and TABLE 22 CHARACTERS' JUMPING ABILITY with the p. 40 modifiers - thief-acrobats and barbarians are particularly skilled in jumping, but ANY character can make a broad jump or a high jump. On the average a running broad jump covers FOUR more feet than a standing one, but it requires a 20-foot run in a straight line toward the obstacle immediately before leaping; without that space or the time to start the run, the standing jump is the best he can do. A high jump covers HALF as much distance horizontally as its height; a flat surface higher than the current elevation is landed on with a roll to absorb the impact; a thin barrier with level ground on the far side demands a successful high jump AND a Dexterity Check - failure lands him in a heap (1d3 damage for a jump of five feet or higher) and he needs the next round to stand up. The die is rolled for EACH jump attempt (a 4th-level character clears a 3-foot high jump only on a 1d3 roll of 3). Table 22: the seven level bands 1-6 through 23+ with the standing broad (1d4+1 to 1d6+6), the running broad (1d4+5 to 1d6+15) and the high jump (1d3 to 1d6+1). Modifiers, cumulative: moderately encumbered -1 foot; heavily encumbered -2 feet and cannot high jump; severely encumbered cannot jump at all; halfling -1 foot on broad jumps only; gnome or dwarf -2 feet broad and -1 foot high - with floors of 2 feet broad and 1 foot high. Census 372 -> 373.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 39-40; the user own copy OCR (pages 40-41) cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0039.djvu with the Guide_0040.djvu head) - the prose reads CLEAN two-way, every number (the four-foot advantage, the 20-foot run, the half-height high jump, the 1d3 five-foot heap damage, the modifier feet and the 2/1 floors) matched exactly; the Table 22 grid is GARBLED in the djvu word layer, so every cell was confirmed by TWO independent IIIF eye-reads of leaf 39 - the OCR and both eye-reads agree on all 21 cells.
banner.sentinel: A running broad jump buys four feet over a standing one but only after a 20-foot straight run; a high jump covers half its height sideways; Table 22 rolls the dice per attempt by level band, and the cumulative encumbrance and demihuman modifiers can never push a jump below two feet broad or one foot high.

consts.name: wjpRunningAdvantageFt
consts.comment: On the average, a character can cover four more feet of distance with a running broad jump than he can with a standing broad jump.

consts.name: wjpRunRequiredFt
consts.comment: A running broad jump requires the character to make a 20-foot run in a straight line toward the obstacle immediately before leaping.

consts.name: wjpHighHorizDiv
consts.comment: A high jump will cover half as much distance horizontally as the height of the jump.

consts.name: wjpHeapDmgDie
consts.comment: Failure on the thin-barrier Dexterity Check indicates the jumper has landed in a heap, possibly causing damage (a 1d3 roll for a jump of five feet or higher).

consts.name: wjpHeapMinFt
consts.comment: The heap damage is possible for a jump of five feet or higher.

consts.name: wjpStandFloorFt
consts.comment: The modifiers are cumulative, but in no case can a broad jump be reduced to less than 2 feet for a character who is otherwise able to make the jump.

consts.name: wjpHighFloorFt
consts.comment: In no case can a high jump be reduced to less than 1 foot for a character who is otherwise able to make the jump.

consts.name: wjpEncModerateFt
consts.comment: Moderately encumbered: -1 foot on jumping ability.

consts.name: wjpEncHeavyBroadFt
consts.comment: Heavily encumbered: -2 feet, and the character cannot high jump at all.

consts.name: wjpHalflingBroadFt
consts.comment: Halfling: -1 foot on broad jumps only.

consts.name: wjpDwarfBroadFt
consts.comment: Gnome or dwarf: -2 feet on broad jumps.

consts.name: wjpDwarfHighFt
consts.comment: Gnome or dwarf: -1 foot on high jumps.

consts.name: wjpBandCount
consts.comment: Table 22 has seven level bands: 1-6, 7-9, 10-12, 13-15, 16-18, 19-22 and 23+.

bools.name: wjpAnyCharacterCanJump
bools.comment: Although thief-acrobats and barbarians are particularly skilled in jumping, any character is capable of making a broad jump or a high jump to get across or over something in his path.

bools.name: wjpRunNeedsStraightRun
bools.comment: A running broad jump requires the 20-foot straight-line run; if this space does not exist or there is no time to back up and start the run, then a standing broad jump is the best he can do.

bools.name: wjpRollToHigherSurface
bools.comment: If the target is a flat surface higher than the character current elevation, he can (if he succeeds in the leap) jump up to the surface and roll to absorb the impact of the jump.

bools.name: wjpThinBarrierDexCheck
bools.comment: If the obstacle is a thin barrier and the surface on the other side is at the same elevation, the jumper must make a successful high jump and then a Dexterity Check.

bools.name: wjpHeapNeedsNextRound
bools.comment: Failure on the check indicates that he has landed in a heap and will need the next round to stand up.

bools.name: wjpDieRolledPerJump
bools.comment: The die is rolled for each jump attempt - a 4th-level character can make a 3-foot high jump if a roll of 1d3 results in a 3, but fails to clear the height on a 1 or 2.

bools.name: wjpModifiersCumulative
bools.comment: The modifiers to jumping ability are cumulative, subject to the 2-foot broad and 1-foot high floors.

bools.name: wjpSevereCannotJump
bools.comment: A severely encumbered character cannot jump at all.

bools.name: wjpHeavyCannotHighJump
bools.comment: A heavily encumbered character cannot high jump (the -2 feet applies to the broad jumps he can still make).

tables.name: Table 22: CHARACTERS' JUMPING ABILITY
col_comments: The standing broad jump die by level band (4 = 1d4, 6 = 1d6): 1d4 for the 1-6 and 7-9 bands, 1d6 for the 10-12 through 23+ bands.
The standing broad jump plus feet by level band: 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 - the 1d4+1 through 1d6+6 ladder.
The running broad jump die by level band (4 = 1d4, 6 = 1d6): 1d4 for the 1-6 and 7-9 bands, 1d6 for the 10-12 through 23+ bands.
The running broad jump plus feet by level band: 5, 6, 5, 6, 9, 12 and 15 - the 1d4+5 through 1d6+15 ladder.
The high jump die by level band (3 = 1d3, 4 = 1d4, 5 = 1d5, 6 = 1d6): 1d3, 1d4, 1d3, 1d4, 1d5, 1d5 and 1d6.
The high jump plus feet by level band: 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1 and 1 - the 1d3 through 1d6+1 ladder.
